## Summary

I implemented rejection of a future `registrationDate` on `POST /api/owners`, returning HTTP 400.

Changes:
1. **`FutureRegistrationDateException.java`** (new) — a `RuntimeException` carrying the offending date, following the same style as the existing `DailyOwnerLimitExceededException`.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — added a check on the raw supplied `registrationDate` (before the business-day roll-forward) that throws `FutureRegistrationDateException` when the value `.isAfter(LocalDate.now())`. Checking the supplied value directly means a future date can never be silently accepted or normalized away. An absent date still defaults to the server date as before.

3. **`ExceptionControllerAdvice`** — added `handleFutureRegistrationDateException`, mapping the exception to `400 Bad Request` with a `ProblemDetail` body whose `errors` array names `registrationDate`, matching the convention used by the other owner-validation handlers.
